notes: All 98 pages read end to end: the preface and preparers, the introduction and methodology with its study-period justification, the three historic-context chapters (the reconstruction period 1906-1915, post-reconstruction expansion 1915-1940, and post-war development to 1978, including its section on racial discrimination and housing access), the architectural characteristics chapter with its building forms, building features and fourteen architectural styles, the evaluation criteria with their integrity and historic-district considerations, the bibliography, and Appendix A. A citywide thematic statement with no inventory table, no APNs and no per-property status codes. Its address-level yield is almost entirely its 55 figure captions, which name a building, a year and the formal or stylistic point it illustrates; the narrative adds two more with named architects. Appendix A lists eleven representative builders and no addresses at all, and the evaluation-criteria chapter names no buildings.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in this document. It states that no in-person field survey was conducted — the reconnaissance was done from Google Street View during the COVID-19 pandemic — and there is no companion inventory.
coverage.note: Numbered San Francisco addresses in 98 pages, all but two of them figure captions. A large share of the buildings it illustrates carry no street number: the captions locate them by block or street instead — Florida Street, Franklin Street north of Filbert, 33rd Avenue north of Clement, Turk Street between Temescal Terrace and Chabot Terrace, Seal Rock Drive, Barcelona Avenue, Locksley Avenue, Connecticut Street south of 20th Street, Graystone Terrace, Duncan Street, Addison Street, Loyola Terrace, Jasper Place and Union Street, Toledo Way, Bay Street, and the intersection of Judah Street and 22nd Avenue. Several of those are the document's best-credited buildings — the Seal Rock Drive flats are Henry Doelger's, the Franklin Street pair James J. Coyle's, the Turk Street penthouse duplexes Rousseau & Company's, the Duncan Street duplexes Merrill Jew's for Elm Associates — and none can become a finding. Two further addresses appear only inside footnotes, as the subjects of Planning case files rather than as claims the statement makes: 3768-70 Fillmore Street and 325-329 Lombard Street.
